south dakota.enforce_note: Non-competes are enforceable only within the limits written into statute: no more than two years and only within a specified county, municipality, or area where the employer still does business.
south dakota.state_note: If any part of the agreement is unreasonable, South Dakota courts will not fix it — the whole agreement is void, and non-competes are voidable for licensed health care workers for contracts signed on or after July 1, 2023.
south dakota.statute_name: Employment Contract — Covenants Not to Compete
south dakota.threshold_note: South Dakota has no earnings threshold, so the two-year and area limits apply to every employee alike.

tennessee.enforce_note: Since July 1, 2026, non-competes are void for employees earning under $70,000 a year, and restrictions of two years or less are presumed reasonable for employees.
tennessee.legal_aid_name: Legal Aid Society of Middle Tennessee and the Cumberlands
tennessee.state_note: The new law applies only to agreements entered into, renewed, or amended on or after July 1, 2026, and it does not ban confidentiality or customer non-solicitation agreements.
tennessee.statute_name: Reasonableness in Time of Restrictive Covenants; Prohibition on Noncompete Agreements for Employees Earning Less Than $70,000 Annually
tennessee.threshold_note: The $70,000 figure is annualized compensation (wages, salary, commissions, and nondiscretionary bonuses), and it is a fixed amount in the statute, not adjusted for inflation.

texas.enforce_note: Non-competes are generally enforceable when they are part of an otherwise enforceable agreement and reasonable in time, geographic area, and scope of activity.
texas.state_note: An overbroad Texas non-compete is usually narrowed by the court rather than thrown out, but since September 1, 2025, physician, dentist, nurse, and physician assistant non-competes are capped at one year, five miles, and a buyout of no more than one year's pay.
texas.threshold_note: Texas has no earnings threshold for non-competes generally, so the reasonableness test applies at every pay level.

utah.enforce_note: Non-competes are enforceable only if they last no more than one year after employment ends and are reasonable, and since May 6, 2026, non-competes with health care workers and veterinarians are banned outright.
utah.state_note: A non-compete longer than one year is void, not just shortened, and an employer that sues to enforce an unenforceable one can be ordered to pay the worker's attorney fees and costs.
utah.threshold_note: Utah has no earnings threshold: the broad $155,000 threshold in 2026 House Bill 203 was tabled and never became law.

vermont.enforce_note: Vermont has no non-compete statute, so courts decide enforceability under a common-law reasonableness test that upholds a covenant unless it is against public policy, unnecessary to protect the employer, or unnecessarily restrictive.
vermont.state_note: Bills to ban non-competes (H.205 in 2025–2026) stalled in committee and never passed, so the court-made reasonableness test is still the whole law.
vermont.threshold_note: With no statute, Vermont has no earnings threshold at all.

virginia.enforce_note: Non-competes are banned for low-wage employees and health care professionals, and higher earners can still be bound only if the agreement is reasonable.
virginia.state_note: An employer that tries to enforce a banned non-compete faces a civil penalty of up to $10,000 per violation, and for agreements signed on or after July 1, 2026, a worker fired without cause cannot be bound unless the employer provides severance or another payment disclosed when the agreement was signed.
virginia.statute_name: Covenants Not to Compete Prohibited; Exceptions; Civil Penalty
virginia.threshold_note: The threshold is Virginia's average weekly wage, recalculated every year by the state, and since July 1, 2025 it also covers every employee entitled to overtime pay regardless of earnings.

washington.enforce_note: Through June 29, 2027, non-competes are void for employees earning $126,858.83 or less in 2026, but a new law voids essentially all non-competes starting June 30, 2027, even ones already signed.
washington.state_note: The employer must give the worker the non-compete terms in writing before the job is accepted, a covenant longer than 18 months is presumed unreasonable, and sale-of-business non-competes survive the 2027 ban.
washington.threshold_note: The employee threshold is adjusted every year for inflation by the Department of Labor and Industries, and the separate threshold for independent contractors is $317,147.09 in 2026.

west virginia.enforce_note: West Virginia has no general non-compete statute, so courts enforce non-competes that are reasonable in time, territory, and activity and necessary to protect a legitimate business interest.
west virginia.state_note: Physicians are the exception: their non-competes are capped by statute at one year and 30 road miles, and are void if the employer fires the physician.
west virginia.threshold_note: With no general statute, West Virginia has no earnings threshold for non-competes.

wisconsin.enforce_note: Non-competes are lawful and enforceable only if the restrictions are reasonably necessary to protect the employer, judged on time, territory, necessity, and fairness to the worker and the public.
wisconsin.state_note: Wisconsin courts will not rewrite an unreasonable non-compete to save it — if any part is unreasonable, the whole covenant is void, and a covenant with no geographic limit at all is void.
wisconsin.threshold_note: Wisconsin has no earnings threshold for non-competes.

wyoming.enforce_note: For contracts entered into on or after July 1, 2025, any non-compete that restricts a person's right to be paid for skilled or unskilled labor is void, with only narrow exceptions.
wyoming.state_note: The ban does not apply to contracts signed before July 1, 2025, which are still judged under court case law, and it does not cover non-competes tied to selling a business, protecting trade secrets, repaying training costs, or executive and management personnel.
wyoming.statute_name: Contractual Provisions in Restraint of Trade Generally Void; Exceptions; Unlawful Intimidation
wyoming.threshold_note: There is no earnings threshold because the ban covers all workers, not just lower-paid ones.
